task.title: Reject blank acceptance criterion descriptions
task.goal: Keep Chora acceptance criteria reviewable by requiring a non-blank description.

requirement.statement: An acceptance criterion must explain what its title means; blank or whitespace-only descriptions are rejected.
constraints: Preserve existing valid acceptance criterion behavior.
Do not change persistence, Public API, UI, Runtime, or Sandbox code.
Return a reviewable patch limited to the declared files.

desired_behavior: NewAcceptanceCriterion accepts a non-blank title and description.
NewAcceptanceCriterion rejects an empty or whitespace-only description.
Task construction and existing Domain tests remain green.
out_of_scope: Changing acceptance criterion IDs or serialization.

criteria.title: Blank descriptions fail closed
criteria.description: Empty and whitespace-only descriptions return domain.ErrInvalidArgument.

criteria.title: Valid criteria remain stable
criteria.description: A valid title and description are retained without unrelated behavior changes.

technical_plan.summary: Tighten the existing AcceptanceCriterion constructor and add focused regression coverage.

steps.description: Add focused constructor tests for valid, empty, and whitespace-only descriptions.
Require a trimmed non-empty description in NewAcceptanceCriterion.
Format both files and run the declared Domain test command.

decisions.question: Which repository task proves the first real coding path?
decisions.resolution: Use the Chora Domain validation task pinned in this contract.
decisions.rationale: It is a real, reviewable product change with a two-file boundary and deterministic tests.

decisions.question: Which Runtime, model, and Sandbox combination enters the amended Entry Probe?
decisions.resolution: Pi Coding Agent 0.84.1 over JSONL RPC with openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol in one disposable Colima-backed Docker container per Attempt.
decisions.rationale: The user replaced only the Task model after the v2 model failed twice; Runtime, Sandbox, base images, configuration, and policy identities remain independently pinned.

decisions.question: How can an Attempt reach OpenAI Codex endpoints without general network access?
decisions.resolution: Attach the Attempt only to an internal private network and route HTTP CONNECT through a task-scoped proxy restricted to auth.openai.com and chatgpt.com on port 443.
decisions.rationale: The boundary resolves DNS, denies IP literals and every undeclared host, does not terminate TLS, and is identified, audited, and removed per Attempt.

decisions.question: How is the user's Pi OpenAI Codex OAuth identity supplied?
decisions.resolution: Require an explicit CHORA_PI_CODEX_AUTH_FILE and project only its openai-codex entry into an Attempt-private 0600 auth.json.
decisions.rationale: The host source is never mounted, no host Pi state is inherited, credential values are never logged or persisted, and refresh failure closes the Attempt without copyback.

risks.description: The selected OpenAI Codex model may fail Pi tool calling or its OAuth session may expire during an Attempt.
risks.mitigation: Record model semantic and authentication failures separately; stop after two semantic failures and fail closed on refresh failure.

risks.description: OAuth material could leak through mounts, environment, events, logs, artifacts, or cleanup failure.
risks.mitigation: Project one provider entry to an Attempt-private file, redact every persisted surface, forbid source mounts and copyback, and require cleanup evidence.

risks.description: A host mount, network route, process, or cleanup mistake could violate the Sandbox boundary.
risks.mitigation: Fail closed on host access, undeclared egress, process-tree death, identity, or cleanup uncertainty.

unknowns.question: Can pinned Pi RPC use the projected OpenAI Codex OAuth entry through the fixed proxy to edit one file and cleanly terminate under the v3 policy?

base_images.purpose: Runtime, boundary, and Chora test stage
